bull_bear.body:
- Three-decade OEM relationships across the US, Europe and India built around complex-geometry, multi-material machined castings under the Magna MasterCAST identity.
- Breadth of quality and marine/pressure-equipment certifications (IATF 16949, PED/AD2000/PESR, DNV, Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas) supports qualification for regulated, high-specification OEM programmes.
- Captive renewable power (windmills plus solar, expanding toward 8.35 MW combined) meeting 73% of FY26 energy needs provides a partial hedge against grid power cost volatility.
- Multiple sand-reclamation technologies, including a Green Sand Reclamation system imported from the UK, positioning the Company as one of few Indian foundries with 3 types of sand reclaim and lowering raw-material consumption.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Trade policy and tariffs — Exports were 47.3% of FY26 revenue, principally to the United States and Europe; tariffs applicable to iron and steel articles and their derivatives affect the delivered cost of the Company's products relative to alternative sources, and may affect order volumes, sourcing decisions and pricing negotiations.
- Logistics and shipping disruption — Export shipments move principally by container from Indian ports; disruption to international shipping routes from geopolitical conflict has reduced container availability and raised freight rates/transit times on the Company's principal export lanes, risking delayed dispatches and higher finished-goods inventory.
- Input and energy cost volatility — Pig iron, steel scrap and ferro alloys, plus energy and fuel inputs (electricity, LPG, diesel), form a substantial part of the cost base; geopolitical-conflict-driven crude oil volatility and any lag in passing cost increases to customers may adversely affect margins.
- Foreign exchange risk — Export receivables are denominated in foreign currency; heightened global macroeconomic uncertainty has increased exchange-rate volatility, and adverse movements may affect reported revenue and margins.
- Skilled workforce availability — Capturing anticipated opportunities in low-to-medium volume engineered castings depends on the availability of skilled engineers and the ability to scale the engineering workforce; the Company flags this as needing to be addressed.
- Cyber security — The Company has cyber security systems in place but is only now planning dedicated audits to enhance and strengthen its defences, indicating an area of evolving exposure.
- Export geographic concentration — Exports are concentrated principally in the United States and Europe, making the Company sensitive to demand conditions and trade policy in those two regions.

- Complete commissioning of a Green Sand Reclamation system imported from the UK, giving the Company 3 types of sand reclaim to minimise sand consumption and conserve natural resources.

- Scale engineering workforce and skilled-labour capability to capture opportunities in low-to-medium volume engineered castings.
- Strengthen cyber security defences through planned audits.
- The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per share (50% of face value) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval, continuing a policy of returning cash to shareholders while funding the recently commissioned Third Moulding Line expansion partly through a term loan and partly through internal accruals; no amount was transferred to the General Reserve during the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Third Moulding Line (Sinto Line) was commissioned on 27 June 2025, lifting total installed moulding capacity to 2000 MT per month, while melting capacity remains at 1500 MT per month and is to be scaled up progressively as new-line production ramps. During the year the Company also installed a 60-litre Cold Box Core Shooter (horizontal-parted) to support larger castings on the Sinto line, commissioned an Eirich sand plant, an Inductotherm auto pouring system and a Wesman sand cooler system, and built a new warehouse of approximately 6,480 sq. ft. at the Factory (North Campus). Future plans set out in the Directors' Report include increasing machining capacity in response to customer demand, commissioning a Green Sand Reclamation system imported from the UK (giving the Company 3 types of sand reclaim), and adding 1.1 MW of solar capacity operational from June 2026, which would take total solar capacity to 5.1 MW and, together with 3.25 MW of windmill capacity, total green energy to 8.35 MW.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's foundry market is projected to grow from approximately USD 26 billion (2025) to approximately USD 47 billion by 2031 (~10% CAGR), a structural industry tailwind.
- China-plus-one supply-chain diversification is creating opportunities for Indian foundries to win business from global OEMs seeking reliable alternative sourcing.
- Rising demand from automobiles, railways, defence, infrastructure, renewable energy and industrial machinery for more precision and high-value castings.
- Export growth opportunity as global supply chains shift toward India for reliable and cost-effective casting supply.
- Newly commissioned Third Moulding Line capacity (2000 MT/month) is expected to be progressively utilised as production scales up, with melting capacity aligned accordingly.
- Countervailing headwinds flagged: higher US tariffs on iron/steel articles and derivatives, tighter trade barriers, cheaper competing imports, high raw-material and energy costs, and shortages of labour and skilled workers.

- Skilled workforce availability — Capturing anticipated opportunities in low-to-medium volume engineered castings depends on the availability of skilled engineers and the ability to scale the engineering workforce; the Company flags this as needing to be addressed.
- Cyber security — The Company has cyber security systems in place but is only now planning dedicated audits to enhance and strengthen its defences, indicating an area of evolving exposure.
- Export geographic concentration — Exports are concentrated principally in the United States and Europe, making the Company sensitive to demand conditions and trade policy in those two regions.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Increase machining capacity to meet rising OEM demand for machined components.
- Complete commissioning of a Green Sand Reclamation system imported from the UK, giving the Company 3 types of sand reclaim to minimise sand consumption and conserve natural resources.
- Expand captive renewable energy generation (solar plus wind) to reduce dependence on grid power.
- Scale engineering workforce and skilled-labour capability to capture opportunities in low-to-medium volume engineered castings.
- Strengthen cyber security defences through planned audits.
- The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per share …

hero.oneLiner: For over three decades, Magna Electro Castings Limited has manufactured low-to-medium volume machined castings (1-250 kg) under the Magna MasterCAST identity for global OEMs in the United States, Europe and India.
